text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it had retracted the licence of Bulgaria's First Private Bank, which was placed in receivership a year ago because it failed to collect loans and repay debts of over 200 billion levs to its creditors.

-- Bulgaria's interim government approved a draft banking law setting stricter regulations aimed to bring local banks up to international standards. Under the draft law the minimum required capital for a bank license is to be set at $6 million.
-- Bulgaria's state fertiliser producer Chimko said it had posted a 35.6 million lev gross profit for the first four months of this year. Chimko's annual net profit is seen at some $20 million.

-- Swiss Glencore International won a tender to import 50,000 tonnes of wheat against exports of this year's harvest, the agriculture ministry said. The tender was held after the private Bulgarian firm Nada which won a tender in March to import 50,000 tonnes of wheat failed to meet its contractual obligations.

-- Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said the expected annual inflation in Bulgaria envisaged in country's 1997 draft budget was about 600 percent, lower than the 769 percent projected under last month's IMF standby accord.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would cut its main interest rate to 4.29 monthly from 5.20 percent monthly effective from Monday.
-- The number of unemployed in Bulgaria rose to 584,851 or 15.3 percent of the workforce in April from 555,835 in March, National Labour Exchange figures showed.
-- Bulgaria may issue a Eurobond denominated in marks by the end of the year, Prime Minister designate Ivan Kostov said.
-- Germany's Advisa Holding and Karsten Oelckers Consulting are interested in buying Bulgaria's private Businessbank, which was placed in receivership by the central bank on September 23.
-- Bulgaria's private First East International Bank said it had posted a 525 million levs gross profit last year.
